1 كَمَحَ الدَّابَّةَ , [aor.
كَمَحَ ,] (inf. n. كَمْحٌ; M) and ↓ أَكْمَحَهَا ; i. q. كَبَحَهَا (A 'Obeyd, K) and أَكْبَحَهَا: (A 'Obeyd:) or كَمَحَ الدَّابَّةَ بِالِلّجَامِ signifies He pulled in the horse, or the like, by the bridle and bit, in order that it might stop, and not run: (M:) and ↓ اكمحها , he pulled its bridle so that its head became upright, or erect. (As, S, M.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
